messages:
marcos: Quick question — new hire accepted. Primary visa is A-3 (diplomatic), spouse has applied for work authorization but EAD is still pending. Start date in 3 weeks. Can we onboard/pay/enroll the spouse without an EAD? Also any special I-9 handling for A-3 holders? cc @people-ops
people-ops: Thanks Marcos. A-visas are a bit special. For the primary we need passport + visa stamp + diplomatic accreditation docs. Spouse employment generally requires work auth (EAD) unless the mission provides a diplomatic note. Benefits-wise we can usually add dependents even if their EAD is pending. Looping in legal to confirm specifics.
immigration-lawyer: Confirming — A-1/A-2/A-3 categories are diplomatic; employment rules vary by country accreditations. If the spouse has a diplomatic accreditation letter that explicitly grants work permission, that can suffice. If not, EAD is required. Please collect the diplomatic note and any I-797C receipts.
ella-hr: For benefits: our carrier allows dependent enrollment without an EAD/SSN. They do request SSN for payroll deductions only. We can add the spouse to medical/dental/vision and set coverage effective immediately or retroactively (carrier dependent).
security-team: Background checks can start now. For I-9 identity verification, we need physical docs. For hires arriving in the US, we can use our third-party I-9 agent to inspect diplomatic IDs/letters in person. If the spouse won't be in the US on day 1, we can't complete their I-9 until they present docs.
marcos: They'll be landing in NYC 2 days before start and will have the accreditation packet. Spouse will be arriving a few days later and EAD is pending. So plan: start primary on day 1 with accreditation shown; onboard spouse to benefits once EAD or diplomatic note is provided. Is that OK? Could we do a short vendor/contractor pay for the spouse for first month if needed?
people-ops: Primary starting is fine once accreditation & passport/visa are verified. We cannot pay someone as an employee without valid work authorization/SSN. Contractor/vendor route is technically possible but has tax/reporting implications and isn't ideal for what should be an employee role. Better to do contingent hire for spouse: hold the offer start until EAD or diplomatic permission, enroll benefits retroactively if needed.
immigration-lawyer: If embassy can issue a diplomatic note granting immediate work permission, send it to us and we'll confirm. If not, we can draft an expedite request template for the EAD based on start-date hardship — but depends on USCIS rules and embassy timelines.
people-ops: Quick checklist to send to candidate/mission:
``n- Primary: passport, A-3 visa stamp, diplomatic accreditation letter (mission brief)
- Spouse: passport, diplomatic note (if any), EAD receipt (I-797C) or EAD card when available
- SSN or SSN application receipt (if already applied)
- Exact arrival dates + point of contact at mission/consulate
```
marcos: :thumbsup: I'll request the docs and ask embassy for a diplomatic note if possible. If spouse ends up on a short consultancy/vendor path for ~2 weeks, is finance ok with that? cc @sam_finance
sam_finance: We can support vendor-pay for short, bona fide contractor engagements with an invoice, but we need procurement approvals and it must be a true vendor relationship. It also triggers different tax/1099 considerations. Not ideal for W-2 work.
marcos: Got it — thanks all. I'll DM when I have scans of the accreditation packet and the spouse's receipt.
